I found two issues. One blocks the PR: a snapshot bump does not include the security fix that triggered it. The other is a missing test and does not block. I executed nothing and read only the diff and the head commit.

## 1. A snapshot bump leaves out the security change that triggered it (blocks)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-1/repo/renovate.json`, line 18 (the `transformTemplates` entry, which ends in `... & $pad($m[0], -2, "0") & "T000000Z"}]})`). It feeds `ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION=20261121T000000Z` at line 11 of `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-1/repo/images/core/Dockerfile`.
- **Reason:** bug, with a security impact.
- **Description:** The transform keeps only the day from the InRelease `Date:` line and sets the time to `000000Z`. That line records when the `resolute-security` pocket last changed, and the change always happens later than midnight of that day. The snapshot service serves the archive as it stood at the requested time. So the proposed snapshot, midnight of that day, is the archive state from just before the change that caused the bump.
- **Guarantee it breaks:** The PR says the snapshot "bumps as soon as the archive changes, since it carries security fixes". The `renovate.json` rule description and ADR 0022 say the same, and the rule drops the release wait for that reason. The latest security fix is never in the image the bump produces. It only arrives with the next bump, which comes the next time the pocket changes, possibly days later.
- **Trigger:** The security pocket publishes a fix at, say, 2026-11-21 13:05 UTC. Its InRelease then reads `Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:05:xx UTC`, and nothing else is published until 2026-11-26.
- **Path:** `renovate.json@customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates` (produces `20261121T000000Z`) → `images/core/Dockerfile@ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION` → `images/core/Dockerfile@RUN echo "APT::Snapshot ..." > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot` → every later `apt-get update`/`install` in the core image and in `images/core-systemd/Dockerfile`. The pin also stays in the image's apt config, so `apt-get install` in CI jobs uses it too.
- **Outcome:** Renovate auto-merges `20261121T000000Z`. Every image, and every `apt-get install` run in a job container, ships the packages from before the 21 Nov fix. That lasts until about 26 Nov, when the next pocket change brings the next bump. On every bump the newest security fix is missing.
- **Fix:** Build the version from the full time on the `Date:` line, e.g. capture `(\d+) (\w{3}) (\d{4}) (\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})` and emit `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`. This loses the "at most one bump a day" property, which is a separate decision. Alternatively, round up to midnight of the next day, but that only works once that time has passed, so a bump would have to wait for the next day.

## 2. No automated test for the snapshot pin (does not block)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-1/repo/images/core/Dockerfile`, line 14: `RUN echo "APT::Snapshot \"${UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION}\";" > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot \`
- **Reason:** missing test for changed behavior.
- **Description:** `docs/usage/core.md` and ADR 0022 say the image keeps the snapshot in apt's config, so `apt-get install` in a job gets that day's versions. Nothing automated checks this. `images/core/smoke.sh` never looks at apt, and the PR checked it only by hand (`apt-cache policy`, two `dpkg-query` runs).
  - If a later change removes or overrides `50snapshot`, apt goes back to floating packages without anyone noticing. A later file in `apt.conf.d` setting `APT::Snapshot` would do it, as would a child image.
  - The same applies if a source stops being served from the snapshot.
- **Fix:** Add a check to `images/core/smoke.sh`. It could assert that `apt-config dump APT::Snapshot` is a non-empty `\d{8}T\d{6}Z` value, and that after an `apt-get update`, `apt-cache policy` lists only `snapshot.ubuntu.com` Ubuntu sources.

## Checked and not raised

- **`containerd.io` pin:** the pattern `containerd.io=${CONTAINERD_VERSION}~*` lines up with `extractVersion=^(?<version>[^~]+)~` and `versioning=deb`. The `deb` package rule now also matches `containerd.io`.
- **Regex manager:** the datasource class `[a-z.-]` accepts `custom.ubuntu-snapshot`. The `versioning=regex:...` value captures correctly, and the `ARG` sits directly below its `# renovate:` comment. The `x.y.0` rule cannot match a snapshot value.
- **JSONata parsing:** the `Date: ` line filter, `$match(...).groups`, the month lookup and the zero padding are correct for RFC 2822 dates.
- **TLS skip:** `Acquire::https::snapshot.ubuntu.com::Verify-Peer=false` applies only to that one host, and only in the first `RUN`, because it is passed with `-o` rather than written to config. Every later update runs after `ca-certificates` is installed.
  - It is not a regression: before this PR the base image fetched over plain `http://archive.ubuntu.com`, with no TLS at all.
  - The custom datasource fetches its InRelease over plain `http://`. A forged `Date:` could at most produce a wrong snapshot PR, which then has to pass CI, so I did not raise it.
- **Other images:** `--error-on=any` is on every `apt-get update` (core and core-systemd). `coder-template` and `devcontainer-base` do not run apt.

## Dismissed findings

None. No reviewer dismissed anything in this pass.

I found two issues: one blocking logic bug in how Renovate works out the snapshot date, and one non-blocking test gap. I read the diff and the head commit only and ran nothing.

### 1. The derived snapshot never includes the latest security change (blocks)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-1/repo/renovate.json`, new line 18, in `customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates`:
  `"($m := $match(releases[$substring(version, 0, 6) = \"Date: \"].version, /(\\d+) (\\w{3}) (\\d{4})/).groups; {\"releases\": [{\"version\": $m[2] & $lookup({...}, $m[1]) & $pad($m[0], -2, \"0\") & \"T000000Z\"}]})"`
- **Reason:** bug (it breaks a stated guarantee, with a security effect).
- **Description:** The transform keeps only the calendar day of the `resolute-security` InRelease `Date:` line and adds `T000000Z`. A snapshot ID is a point in time: `snapshot.ubuntu.com` serves the archive as it stood at that moment. A pocket published during day D has a `Date:` later than 00:00 that day, so `<D>T000000Z` is the archive just before that publish. The pin therefore always lags one publish behind. The fix that triggered the bump is the one fix it leaves out, and it only arrives when the pocket next changes on a later day.

  This breaks guarantees the PR states in several places:
  - The PR body says the latest snapshot "is the day the resolute-security pocket last changed".
  - The `packageRules` description says "it carries security fixes".
  - ADR 0019 says it "bumps as soon as the archive changes, since it carries security fixes".
  - ADR 0022 says Renovate proposes a newer snapshot "at most once a day".
- **Trigger:** Ubuntu publishes a security update to `resolute-security` at any time after 00:00 UTC, so the InRelease reads something like `Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:32:11 UTC`. The pocket then stays unchanged for one or more days, which is normal on weekends.
- **Path:**
  1. `renovate.json@customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates` produces `20261121T000000Z`.
  2. Through `customManagers[0].matchStrings` this becomes the new `UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION` in `images/core/Dockerfile@ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION`.
  3. That value is written to `images/core/Dockerfile@RUN echo "APT::Snapshot ..."` (`/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot`).
  4. Every later `apt-get update` reads the snapshot at 2026-11-21 00:00:00 UTC. That covers the python3 and docker steps in core, `images/core-systemd/Dockerfile@RUN apt-get update --error-on=any`, and CI jobs using the image.
- **Outcome:** Renovate automerges a "bump" whose packages do not include the 14:32 security update. While the pocket stays quiet, Renovate proposes nothing more, because the derived version is unchanged. The fixed packages stay out of every image, child image and `apt-get install` in a job until the next security publish on a later day. The same pattern holds in steady state: each bump misses its own day's fixes.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the full `Date:` timestamp (`YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`) as the version. Day granularity alone does not limit bumps to one a day, and ordering under the existing regex versioning still works. If one bump a day is wanted, schedule Renovate for that instead of truncating the timestamp.
- **Related, also under this finding:** Only `-security` is watched, so a change published only to `-updates` never moves the pin. ADR 0019 says "as soon as the archive changes", which is broader than what the code watches.

### 2. No test checks the apt snapshot pin (non-blocking)

- **File:** `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/repo` is not the path; the file is `/tmp/pr-review-eval-7c1e/runs/images83fix-p8-1/repo/images/core/Dockerfile`, new line 14:
  `RUN echo "APT::Snapshot \"${UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION}\";" > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot \`
  The missing test belongs in `images/core/smoke.sh`.
- **Reason:** missing test.
- **Description:** `docs/usage/core.md` and ADR 0022 promise that the image keeps the snapshot in apt's config, so that `apt-get install` in a job gets "the versions of that day". No smoke script checks this, so if a later change removes or overwrites `50snapshot`, CI stays green. The PR's test plan checked it once, by hand, with `apt-cache policy`.
- **Suggested fix:** In `images/core/smoke.sh`, assert that `apt-config dump APT::Snapshot` (or `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/50snapshot`) holds a value matching `^\d{8}T\d{6}Z$`.

### Checked and not raised
- **TLS peer check turned off for `snapshot.ubuntu.com` in the first step:** this is no regression. The step used plain http to `archive.ubuntu.com` before, apt still checks InRelease signatures and hashes, and the setting applies to that one RUN only.
- **Plain-http InRelease fetch by Renovate:** someone tampering with it could only choose a date. Regex versioning ignores an older date, so I found no concrete harm.
- **containerd.io pin:** `"containerd.io=${CONTAINERD_VERSION}~*"`, the `extractVersion`, and adding it to the deb `packageRules` look consistent.
- **Child images:** `devcontainer-base` and `coder-template` have no apt steps. `core-systemd` inherits `50snapshot`.
- **Build cache:** the ARG is used in the RUN, so a bump invalidates the cache for later layers.
- **`"minimumReleaseAge": null`:** if `null` did not clear the global "3 days", the custom datasource, which gives no release timestamp, would be held forever. I could not confirm Renovate's behaviour from its docs, so I did not flag it.

Dismissed findings to log for human review: none.

review.body: The snapshot pin, the `--error-on=any` hardening, the `containerd.io` revision pin and the Renovate wiring hang together, and the PR title and description match the change. One blocking issue: the custom datasource turns the security pocket's `Date:` into midnight of that day. So every snapshot bump misses the very security update that triggered it, which breaks the stated reason for skipping the release wait. One non-blocking gap: no smoke check covers the snapshot the image now keeps in apt's config.

comments.body:
**Blocking: a bump leaves out the security update that triggered it.**

The transform keeps only the day from the `resolute-security` InRelease `Date:` line and appends `T000000Z`. `snapshot.ubuntu.com` serves the archive as it stood at that instant. A publish on day D always has a `Date:` after 00:00 on D, so `<D>T000000Z` is the archive just *before* that publish.

- **Trigger:** a security update is published at, say, `Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:32:11 UTC`, and the pocket then stays quiet for a few days.
- **Path:** `renovate.json@customDatasources.ubuntu-snapshot.transformTemplates` yields `20261121T000000Z` → `images/core/Dockerfile@ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT_VERSION` → `images/core/Dockerfile@RUN echo "APT::Snapshot ..."` (`50snapshot`) → every later `apt-get update` in core, core-systemd and CI jobs.
- **Outcome:** Renovate automerges a bump whose packages do not include the 14:32 fix. The derived version then stays the same, so nothing more is proposed until the pocket changes on a later day. Each bump misses its own day's fixes. This contradicts the stated reason for skipping the release wait ("it carries security fixes" in this rule's description, and "bumps as soon as the archive changes" in ADR 0019).

**Suggested fix:** emit the full timestamp from the `Date:` line, by capturing `(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})` as well and building `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`; the existing regex versioning still orders it. If you still want at most one bump a day, enforce that with a Renovate `schedule` rather than by truncating the time.

**Non-blocking: no test covers the snapshot pin.**

`docs/usage/core.md` and ADR 0022 promise that the image keeps the snapshot in apt's config, so `apt-get install` in a job gets that day's versions. `images/core/smoke.sh` never checks this; the test plan verified it once, by hand, with `apt-cache policy`. If a later change drops, renames or overrides `50snapshot`, apt silently goes back to floating packages and CI stays green.

**Suggested fix:** in `images/core/smoke.sh`, assert that `apt-config dump APT::Snapshot` holds a value matching `^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z$`.
